answer: Tie each agent to a real FIDE chess rating. The agent links its FIDE ID, the network checks the rating against the public FIDE database, and one rating backs one agent. A recheck each quarter demands a new rated game within 90 days, so a dormant account freezes. Building one fake rating takes five rated games against rated players, entry fees near $50 a tournament plus travel. Faking 1,000 agents costs about $50,000 and needs 1,000 real humans sitting at boards. A rating history grows slow like a vine around a marble king, and the whole atlas of games shows who really played.
